title: Part Five: The Scofield Reference Bible

sections.brief: The book as an object: OUP 1909 via Frowde and the New York branch (Armstrong); notes on the same page as the KJV text; seven consulting editors (Sandeen); the 1917 revision (dates, Ussher; the Balfour-reference claim tested and dropped); sales (two million by 1945; 1,925,000 in thirty years; not 'tens of millions'); the 1967 New Scofield committee and changes; later editions and public-domain notes. Figures: time; stats

What the 1917 notes actually say: Gen 12:1/15:18 (unconditional covenant; 'fared ill' with persecutors; land; third dispersion), Deut 30:3 Palestinian Covenant sequence (return of the Lord before restoration), Rom 11 (Israel not set aside; remnant in tribulation; Church does not inherit Jewish promises), Ezek 38 (Russia, Moscow and Tobolsk); what the notes do not say (no state, no political programme, no Balfour); how later teachers restated them (Hagee); 'prerequisite' claim tested. Figure: compare

Who paid: Ball, Pirie, Buss, Fitch (Gaebelein 1943, via Scofield-Files, Dunlap, Goeman), Scofield's own acknowledgment of Ball and Pirie (Rushing via Check Your Fact), Lyman Stewart $1,000 1908 (Sandeen, via Scofield-Files, unchecked), OUP's commercial role; the Untermyer claim from Canfield's 'we assume' (1988) through Lutz (2005) and WRMEA (2015), and the Rothschild variant from Piper (2004); four reasons it fails; the trope named; stated positions of fact-checkers and proponents. Figures: money; time
